Create a validated growth data object

Source: R/core-data.R
wgh_data.Rd

wgh_data() is the entry point of the package's data contract. It maps the columns of a user's data frame to standard roles (id, age, sex, height, weight, site, year), checks types and units, orders the visits within each child and records the mapping so outputs can be relabelled in the user's own terms. Columns not named in the mapping are kept unchanged.

Usage

wgh_data(
  data,
  id,
  sex,
  age = NULL,
  dob = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  site = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  bmi = NULL,
  age_unit = c("years", "months", "days"),
  age_from = c("auto", "age", "dates"),
  date_format = NULL,
  check = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per child visit.

id, sex

Child identifier and sex (any common coding such as "Male"/"Female", "M"/"F" or 1/2).

age

Age at measurement (optional when dob and date are given).

dob, date

Date of birth and date of measurement. Dates, or character strings in a format readable by as.Date() (see date_format).

height, weight

Height in cm and weight in kg (optional).

site, year

Recruitment site and calendar (or school) year (optional). When year is not given but date is, the calendar year of the measurement is used.

bmi

Optional existing BMI column. When absent and both height and weight are present, BMI is computed.

age_unit

Unit of age: "years" (default), "months" or "days".

age_from

"auto", "age" (use the age column only) or "dates" (always compute age from dob and date).

date_format

Format passed to as.Date() when dates are stored as text, for example "%d/%m/%Y". The default reads ISO dates ("2024-09-15").

check

If TRUE (default), run plausibility checks and report them.

Value

An object of class wgh_data: a list with the standardised data ($data), the column mapping ($map) and a log of checks ($log). The data always contain id, age (years) and sex, plus any mapped roles, bmi when height and weight are present, and the original columns that were not mapped.

Details

Age can be given directly (age) or computed from the date of birth (dob) and the date of measurement (date). With age_from = "auto" (default) a supplied age column is used and missing ages are filled in from the dates. With age_from = "dates" age is always computed from the dates, which is the most accurate choice when both dates are recorded. Exact age in years is (date - dob) / 365.25.

Arguments are given as bare column names (tidy evaluation). id, sex and either age or both dob and date are required.

Next steps

Pass the object to wgh_clean() for cleaning, wgh_add_zscores() for WHO or CDC z-scores, wgh_classify() for nutritional status and wgh_sample_flow() to record the analytic sample. Every function in the package accepts a wgh_data object or a plain data frame.

See also

wgh_clean(), wgh_add_zscores(), wgh_sample_flow()

Examples

# Age already recorded
gd <- wgh_data(growdat, id = pid, age = age, sex = sex, height = height,
               weight = weight, site = site, year = yearvisit)
gd
#> <wgh_data>: 8663 visits from 3259 children
#> Ages 1.5 to 18.49 years. Sex: Male 4625, Female 4038
#> Sites: Site1, Site2, Site3
#> Years: 2018 to 2025
#> Mapping: id = pid, age = age, sex = sex, height = height, weight = weight, site
#> = site, year = yearvisit
summary(gd)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   children visits visits_per_child_median age_min age_max  male female
#>      <int>  <int>                   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <int>  <int>
#> 1     3259   8663                       2     1.5    18.5  1720   1539

# Age computed from date of birth and date of measurement
gd2 <- wgh_data(growdat, id = pid, sex = sex, dob = dob, date = examdate,
                height = height, weight = weight, site = site)
head(gd2$data[, c("id", "dob", "date", "age", "year")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   id      dob        date         age  year
#>   <chr>   <date>     <date>     <dbl> <int>
#> 1 C000001 2016-10-24 2019-10-25  3.00  2019
#> 2 C000001 2016-10-24 2020-09-18  3.90  2020
#> 3 C000001 2016-10-24 2022-12-10  6.13  2022
#> 4 C000001 2016-10-24 2023-11-29  7.10  2023
#> 5 C000001 2016-10-24 2024-11-26  8.09  2024
#> 6 C000001 2016-10-24 2025-10-24  9.00  2025

# Dates stored as day/month/year text
df <- data.frame(child = c("a", "a"), gender = c("F", "F"),
                 birth = c("01/03/2015", "01/03/2015"),
                 visit = c("15/09/2022", "20/09/2023"), ht = c(124.0, 130.2))
wgh_data(df, id = child, sex = gender, dob = birth, date = visit, height = ht,
         date_format = "%d/%m/%Y")$data
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   id    sex      age dob        date        year height
#>   <chr> <fct>  <dbl> <date>     <date>     <int>  <dbl>
#> 1 a     Female  7.54 2015-03-01 2022-09-15  2022   124 
#> 2 a     Female  8.56 2015-03-01 2023-09-20  2023   130.
